title: Consolidation Amount for Value Carried onto a Card by Replacement
content:
**Accounting rule — Gift Cards & Store Credit.** For value that reached the moving card by a replacement, the carried value is the amount the replacement transfer-out entry on the stolen or lost card moved onto it. The move limit is 60.00. The consolidation amount is the carried value capped at the move limit, the rest staying on the moving card, in US dollars to the cent.

## Terms

- **Moving card.** The card the value is moved off in the consolidation.
- **Stolen or lost card.** The locked card whose replacement transfer-out entry moved its value onto the moving card; the carried value is read from that entry on its ledger.
- **Move limit.** The most that moves in the consolidation: 60.00.
- **Consolidation amount.** The lower of the carried value and the move limit; whatever the cap holds back stays on the moving card.

## Worked figures (hypothetical consolidations)

| Carried value | Move limit | Consolidation amount | Left on the moving card from the carried value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 85.20 | 60.00 | 60.00 | 25.20 |
| 60.00 | 60.00 | 60.00 | 0.00 |
| 42.00 | 60.00 | 42.00 | 0.00 |

## Point of judgement

The carried value is the figure on the stolen or lost card's replacement transfer-out entry, not the moving card's current balance: spending or other loads on the moving card since the replacement do not change it.
